remaining_findings.requirement: C-2: Tree lives only in JS memory of WKWebView
remaining_findings.detail: User-spec says 'lives only in JS memory of WKWebView, not saved to SQLite'. The actual design stores the canonical tree in Swift (InsightSession/InsightNode). Decision 3 states no SQLite and ARC-frees on tab close, which satisfies the user-facing constraint, but does not acknowledge the divergence from user-spec wording. A reader comparing user-spec to tech-spec encounters an unexplained contradiction. Decision 3 should note that 'JS memory' in user-spec was an implementation assumption the team refined — canonical tree is Swift-side, JS holds only rendered snapshots. No impact on implementation correctness.

remaining_findings.requirement: Streaming pipeline: setInsightDeepDives and showInsightLoading trigger conditions unspecified
remaining_findings.detail: The streaming pipeline diagram (Architecture section) shows JS handles topic rendering autonomously via the ---DEEP-DIVES--- marker parser inline during appendInsightDelta processing. Neither setInsightDeepDives nor showInsightLoading appears in the pipeline diagram. No Decision, no task description, and no Acceptance Criteria bullet specifies when Swift would call setInsightDeepDives (given JS already renders topics from the marker) or when showInsightLoading fires relative to appendInsightDelta. Task 6 lists both as commands to implement but provides no trigger condition. These two commands risk being implemented in Task 6 and never called. The spec should either (a) define a specific trigger for each command with a code path that invokes it, or (b) explicitly remove them and confirm JS autonomously handles loading state and topic rendering via the streaming path.

summary: Both R2 critical findings are closed. F-1: InsightSession data model now includes retryCurrent() async and private handleStreamError(_:) with the retry-throttle note — the canonical interface is in sync with Decision 11 and Task 4 prescriptions. F-2: Architecture section WebViewBridge entry now correctly states 5 Swift→JS commands and 5 JS→Swift message types, matching Task 6 exactly. Cross-section consistency check passes: Architecture, Data Models, Implementation Tasks, and Acceptance Criteria all agree on the 5-message protocol and the full retry path. Tab-switch and retry-throttle acceptance criteria are present. Two minor carry-forward findings remain (F-3: user-spec JS-memory wording not reconciled in Decision 3; F-4: setInsightDeepDives and showInsightLoading have no specified trigger condition in the streaming pipeline). Neither blocks implementation. Verdict: PASS.
